Now I see the pattern:
1. Blob was at 67 pixels, now at 65 pixels (shrank by 2)
2. Magenta square moved from (26, 28) to (26, 36) - from left side to right side of blob
3. Blob boundary changed on the right side
So clicking on the right side of the blob moved the magenta square from the left side to the right side. The blob shrank by 2 pixels (from 67 to 65).
Wait, let me reconsider. When I clicked on the LEFT side of the blob:
- Blob grew from 65 to 67 pixels (+2)
- Square moved from inside blob to left side (26, 28)
When I clicked on the RIGHT side of the blob:
- Blob shrank from 67 to 65 pixels (-2)
- Square moved from left side (26, 28) to right side (26, 36)
Hmm, so the blob doesn't just expand/contract. The square is being moved around the blob. Let me think about this differently.
Maybe the mechanic is:
- Clicking on the blob moves the absorbed square to that side of the blob
- The blob's shape changes to accommodate the square's new position
So the square at (26, 32) was inside the blob. When I clicked at (27, 29) [left side], the square moved to (26, 28) [left of blob]. When I clicked at (27, 37) [right side], the square moved to (26, 36) [right of blob].
This suggests that clicking on the blob moves the absorbed square to that position. The blob's shape changes to accommodate this.
But what's the goal? Maybe the goal is to move the absorbed square to a specific position? Or maybe the goal is to use the blob to "push" squares around?
Let me think about this more carefully. The blob has one absorbed square inside it. When I click on different parts of the blob, the square moves to that position. This is like the blob is a "carrier" that can move the square around.
Maybe the goal is to move the absorbed square to one of the other squares' positions, or to a specific target?
Actually, let me look at the colored squares at the top-left again: S, M, p, Y. These are at columns 1, 5, 9, 13. Maybe the goal is to move the absorbed square to one of these positions?
But that would take many actions. Let me think about this differently.
Actually, maybe the goal is simpler. Maybe the goal is to move the absorbed square to the position of one of the colored squares at the top. The colored squares are S (sky blue), M (magenta), p (purple), Y (yellow). The magenta square (M) is at column 5. Maybe the goal is to move the absorbed magenta square to column 5?
But the square can only be moved by clicking on the blob, and the blob is at columns 29-37. So the square can only be moved within the blob's range.
Hmm, let me try a different approach. Let me click on the TOP of the blob to see if the square moves up.

print("Current magenta squares:")
for n in nodes:

        print(f"  boundary={n['boundary']}")

print("\nBlue blob:")
for n in nodes:

        print(f"  pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")

if last_transition and last_transition.before_frame:

    print("\nBefore - blue blob:")
    for n in before:
        if n['color'] == 'b':
            print(f"  pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")

</function>
